title: Two housing developments approved, water funding advanced
subtitle: Water financial plans, Columbia Street watermain funding, 2025 surplus projection, and a first look at a Westhill Drive apartment proposal.
overview: Council approved two major land-use applications. One is a residential subdivision with a park, commercial block and stormwater pond at 400 Millennium Blvd, on land formerly designated for employment uses. The other is a nine-storey apartment building at 1 Dunbar Road North. Both passed {{vote:m8}} and {{vote:m9}}. They add housing, but residents raised concerns about traffic, parking, shadowing and loss of farmland.

Council also advanced water and finance items. It directed staff to submit the water and sanitary financial plans to the province in support of the drinking water licence renewal {{vote:m4}}. It released capital funding for the Columbia Street watermain replacement {{vote:m7}}. It acknowledged projected 2025 tax-base and enterprise surpluses, with a final allocation report due by May 2026 {{vote:m5}}.

Council held an informal public meeting on a proposed eight- and six-storey apartment development at 36 Westhill Drive. No decision was made, and staff will report back later. Council also heard that a report on a special service area levy vote was deferred to November 3, 2025. Before the evening session, council met in closed session on training, land acquisition and potential litigation. The minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved an Official Plan amendment, zoning change and draft plan of subdivision for the Activa Holdings lands, and delegated draft-approval conditions and final registration to the Director of Planning.
Council approved an Official Plan amendment and zoning change to allow a nine-storey apartment building at 1 Dunbar Road North.
Council released $2,258,000 in 2025 capital funding and $2,398,000 in 2026 funding for the Columbia Street watermain replacement between King Street North and Old Post Road.
Council directed staff to submit the water distribution and sanitary financial plans to the province by December 4, 2025, in support of the drinking water licence renewal.
Council acknowledged a projected 2025 net tax base surplus of $586,000 and an enterprise surplus of about $628,000, and asked for a final allocation report by May 2026.
Council received the drinking water management review and operational plan update for information.

debate: On Columbia Street, councillors asked about timing of the bike lanes and pedestrian crossings, and one pressed for the road to stay open during construction. Staff said they do not install water stubs for undefined future development, citing the risk of dead-end pipes. They estimated a full closure of two to three weeks, subject to detailed design.

On the Westhill Drive proposal, councillors asked about the lack of play or green space, drainage on a sloped site, headlights from the parking structure, noise from heat pumps and the traffic study scope. Staff agreed to consider including the nearby roundabout in the study. The applicant said servicing costs and financing requirements drive the density. A resident raised traffic, drainage and the combined effect of nearby towers.

On 400 Millennium Blvd, councillors asked about Millennium Boulevard crossings, traffic calming and noise study assumptions. They also asked about winter salt on a trail beside protected natural areas and a First Nation's request for a wider buffer. Staff said reorienting blocks would narrow the park too much. A delegate for nearby residents raised concerns about traffic, parking at RIM Park events, density and loss of farmland and wildlife.

On 1 Dunbar Road North, staff said shadows were modestly greater than a six-storey building would cast but not adverse. The applicant said setbacks were increased and the building reshaped over the past year. A resident said an updated shadow study was hard to find online, and staff agreed to separate shadow studies from architectural drawings in future.
